reading.body:
Google operates a long-running data center campus in Berkeley County (Moncks Corner), South Carolina, but publishes no capacity figure for this individual facility. The company announced a $500 million expansion specific to Moncks Corner and a combined $3.3 billion expansion across two South Carolina campuses in September 2024, yet has not disclosed megawatts, square footage, or exact addresses for buildings at the site.

Google does not publish individual building specifications for any of its data centers, only aggregate state-level investment figures on its official location pages. This means the actual power draw, rack count, and accelerator capacity at this Berkeley County campus cannot be determined from public sources. Researchers assessing AI infrastructure must work from investment announcements rather than operational capacity data.

South Carolina has 14 mapped data center facilities across the state, of which only 4 have published megawatt figures totaling 6.6 MW. This Berkeley County campus ranks fifth among published capacity sites in the state, though its actual power consumption remains undisclosed. The gap between facility count and published capacity is typical for the state and reflects operator policies limiting transparency on individual site specifications.
